submission.natural_language_explanation: The direction fires on a short subword fragment that opens or sits inside a word the tokenizer has split, before the word is complete: most strongly the bare letter token ' A'/'A'/' a' starting a rare name, acronym or foreign word (' A'|arhus, ' A'|ED|C, '('A|UA, ' a'|prof|undamento), and also mid-word pieces of rare technical or foreign words ('ke'|'ph'|alin, 'é'|'th'|ique) and a LaTeX ' $' opening an inline symbol. Whole common words (Oslo, dopamine, Google, the bank) stay weak (below about 0.25 of max), and a stand-alone article or verb ' a' is moderate (about 0.4 to 0.75 of max).

Broader: a general rare-word or tokenizer-uncertainty signal that fires on every piece of any word split into several subword tokens, including the last piece and common multi-token words; it predicts final pieces such as 'arhus' or 'alin' fire as strongly as the opening fragment.
